transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep having these evenings where I’ll buy a family-size takeout meal, plus chips or bakery stuff from the store, and eat most of it myself. It’s like I don’t even realize how much I’ve eaten until it’s already gone.
After one of these episodes where you eat a large amount, do you ever try to get rid of the food or 'make up for it'—like making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
I’m not really sure what you mean by “make up for it.” I know I feel bad afterward, but I haven’t really thought of it that way.
After one of these eating episodes, have you ever made yourself vomit or felt the urge to?
No, I haven’t made myself throw up. I feel pretty upset afterward, but I don’t do that.
Over the past three months, how often would you say these binge-eating episodes have been happening—roughly how many times per week?
Looking back at my journal, I’ve barely had a week in the last few months without at least one. Most weeks, it happens several times.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?
Yes. Once I start, it feels like a switch flips. I can be telling myself, “Taylor, put it away,” but my hands just keep opening containers. It feels like I’m not the one in charge anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes (several times per week for at least 3 months) of eating unusually large amounts of food (family-size takeout plus additional snacks) with a subjective sense of loss of control over eating.
